evidence: Verified in 20e9895 that main.ts built the observation set as `for (const pane of snapshot.panes) sessions.add(pane.sessionId)` with no owned-session filter, so the owned session got a follower on top of the primary already attached to it; fef154f adds `if (pane.sessionName === TMUX_SESSION_NAME) continue;`. Duplicate %output for owned panes was real.
guidance_note: When wiring a snapshot into a component that already covers one member of that snapshot itself, write the owned-vs-foreign partition at the wiring site in the same edit that creates the projection.

evidence: Verified `this.observed` in 20e9895 is assigned at exactly one line (197, inside observeSessions) and read nowhere. The reviewer offered two remedies - remove it, or use it to drive respawn after unexpected exits - and the agent removed it, arguing the topology snapshot was the only legitimate writer; two rounds later (F12) the same reviewer showed snapshot-only respawn cannot work because topology broadcast is diff-gated, and 16c05e9 reintroduced `this.observed` with a reader.
guidance_note: When a finding offers remove-it-or-implement-it, pick by asking whether a reader is required for correctness; deleting unread state does not delete the requirement that created it.

evidence: Read on() in 20e9895: the returned unsubscribe calls `follower.client.off(event, handler)` but never removes the closure pushed into `follower.listenerDisposers`, so the array grows with every subscribe/unsubscribe cycle and teardown iterates stale entries. The agent did not take the reviewer's Map suggestion; it deleted listenerDisposers and derived the detach pass from `this.listeners` at teardown time, which removes the drift by construction.
guidance_note: When a subscribe path stores per-target cleanup state, make the unsubscribe path the exact inverse in the same edit, or derive teardown from the registry instead of storing it twice.

evidence: The FollowerClient comment in 20e9895 names an auto-respawn-on-exit path that the shuttingDown flag supposedly protects, while the exit handler at line 428 only deletes the map row and disposes listeners; no respawn exists in that commit. The comment described an abandoned design.
guidance_note: When a mechanism is dropped late in the design (in-handler respawn replaced by snapshot-driven respawn), grep the file for the abandoned mechanism's name and rewrite every comment that references it before pushing.

evidence: Same defect as F1 in the integration test's own onSnapshot wiring, which claimed to replicate the production path but omitted the filter; the agent mirrored the production filter and added an appears-exactly-once assertion on an owned-session marker. The cited law decorates a test-mirroring change - no mode or branch was collapsed by it.
guidance_note: When a test says it replicates production wiring, diff it against the production wiring line by line and add an exactly-once assertion so a duplicated stream fails the test instead of passing silently.

evidence: The reviewer's literal claim - that widening transportFactory to `(target: string) => TmuxTransport` breaks `npm run typecheck` at zero-arg call sites - is false: TypeScript accepts a function with fewer parameters wherever a wider signature is expected, and the agent reported verifying a clean typecheck. The underlying risk was real - a zero-arg test factory silently ignores the target and attaches to the owned session - and the agent updated all three integration-test factories anyway.
guidance_note: When a factory signature gains a parameter, make every existing factory consume it in the same commit rather than relying on TypeScript's arity tolerance to keep the tree green.

evidence: The phrase `the primary's attached session is observed like any other` is byte-identical in 20e9895 and fef154f, and it was TRUE in 20e9895 - main.ts passed every session id including the owned one. F1's fix added the owned-session filter, which is what made the comment false; 6578e66's own message says so.
guidance_note: When a fix changes which component covers a case, grep for comments asserting the old coverage and rewrite them inside the fix commit.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: I diffed src/main/tmux/output-router.ts between 20e9895 and fef154f and the header block is identical (fef154f does not touch the file). The stale line - `The pause/continue auto-resume follows the same pattern: receive -> broadcast state -> resume` - was already wrong in the original PR commit, which is the commit that moved auto-resume into the connection.
guidance_note: When a commit moves a responsibility out of a class, rewrite that file's header comment in the same commit as the move, not when a reviewer notices.

evidence: Flag is a false positive: the header block claiming `connect() and spawnFollower() run the same sequence ... setStatus(connecting) -> ... -> setStatus(ready)` is verbatim in 20e9895, and 6578e66 changed only the spawnPrimaryClient inline comment (I read the commit diff). spawnFollower never touched status in any commit, so the generalization was false from the start.
guidance_note: When a law-annotated header generalizes two code paths into one sequence, check each path actually performs every step named before writing the generalization.

evidence: The asymmetry is real - the follower exit handler in 20e9895 deletes the map row without calling client.close(), unlike handlePrimaryFailure and tearDownFollower - but the transport has already dropped by then, so the reviewer's leaked-process claim is speculative; the agent conceded as much (mostly defensive). Not fix-caused: the missing close() is present in 20e9895; fef154f only removed the disposer loop from that same handler. Citing single-enforcer for adding a second close call site is a token pasted onto a symmetry preference.
guidance_note: Write the unexpected-drop path and the deliberate-teardown path as the same cleanup sequence when you first write them, so the two do not diverge on which resources get released.

evidence: 6578e66 - the commit whose entire purpose was `fix stale comments after the refactor` and which rewrote output-router.ts's auto-resume claim for F8 - touched only control.ts and output-router.ts (verified with git show --stat); the identical stale claim in output-router.test.ts's Coverage focus header survived, and cost round 3 on its own.
guidance_note: When fixing a stale claim in one file, grep the repo for the phrase and fix every hit in that commit; a same-subsystem test header is the likeliest second hit.

evidence: Verified the reviewer's premise in TmuxTopologyTracker.broadcast: `const json = JSON.stringify(panes); if (json === this.lastBroadcastJson) return;` - an unchanged pane list never reaches listeners, so a follower whose transport dies without perturbing topology is never respawned. F2's fix deleted `this.observed` (the reviewer had offered using it to drive exactly this respawn); 16c05e9 reintroduced the field plus a 500ms per-session timer.
guidance_note: Before relying on a downstream event as a recovery trigger, read that producer's emit condition - a diff-gated broadcaster is not a heartbeat and cannot carry a liveness requirement.

evidence: 16c05e9 (F12's fix) changed follower recovery from snapshot-driven to timer-driven and touched only control.ts and control.test.ts (git show --stat), leaving docs/tmux-integration-plan.md asserting `the next snapshot respawns it` - a claim the same commit had just made false.
guidance_note: When a fix changes a mechanism a design doc describes, update the doc in the fix commit; the doc is part of the blast radius of a behavior change.

evidence: Verified 16c05e9 added exactly one scheduleFollowerRespawn call site - inside the client.on(exit) handler - while spawnFollower has three failure exits (transport-factory throw, setFlags reject, unexpected exit). 45d4b4e then added the other two, one round later.
guidance_note: When adding a recovery call to one failure path, enumerate every early-return and rejection path in that function and give them all the same recovery posture in the same commit.

evidence: The header sentence `follower failures only log and rely on the next topology snapshot for reconciliation` was written by 4d03ea3 (F9's fix) and invalidated by 16c05e9 (F12's fix), which introduced the timer respawn without touching it - I read both diffs. Third stale-comment finding in this PR traceable to a fix commit.
guidance_note: A behavior-changing fix should end with a re-read of the file header it just contradicted, since the header is where the previous fix wrote the policy being replaced.

evidence: The reconnectDelayMs comment `followers are respawned by the next observeSessions() reconciliation` dates from 20e9895 and went stale at 16c05e9; 45d4b4e (F15's fix) rewrote the identical claim in the same file's header 45 lines above and left this one, which is what round 6 spent a comment on.
guidance_note: When a comment-sweep finding lands, sweep the whole file for the claim rather than the flagged line - the same sentence usually appears in the options block and the header.

evidence: Before 16c05e9 there was no respawn timer at all, so the storm the reviewer describes - every observed session re-attempting attach-session every 500ms while the tmux server is down - is behavior introduced by F12's fix, and 45d4b4e widened it to two more failure paths. The agent's fix gates scheduling on primary readiness, but its stated recovery path (a fresh topology snapshot once primary is ready) leans again on the diff-gated broadcast that F12 established is unreliable, so an isolated primary drop with an unchanged pane list can still leave a follower dark. The cited law argues against silent degradation; it is pasted onto a deliberate deferral.
guidance_note: When adding a retry timer, gate it on the health of the dependency it retries against in the same commit, and check that the convergence path you name is not the one you just proved unreliable.

narrative: Eight rounds and seventeen findings on a PR the author closed unmerged the next morning with the comment `This was an invalid architectural design`, replaced by #5. Rounds 0-2 were genuine defects in the original commit (owned-session double-follower, dead state, disposer leak, three stale headers). Rounds 3-6 were almost entirely self-inflicted: F2's fix deleted the state the reviewer had offered as the alternative remedy, which produced F12 four rounds later, and F12's fix then produced a doc drift (F13), a two-of-three-paths omission (F14), a stale header (F15) and a genuine new retry-storm bug (F17), with F16 falling out of F15's incomplete sweep. Seven of the seventeen findings are comment or doc staleness, five of those traceable to a fix commit. Every finding was accepted; the single partial pushback (F6) was correct on the merits and the agent applied the fix anyway.
guidance_observations: A fix commit that changes a behavior policy should end by re-reading the file header, the options block, and the design doc that stated the old policy, because in this PR each of those produced its own review round.
When a reviewer offers two remedies (remove this state, or give it a reader), choosing the cheaper one without checking whether the requirement still needs a reader cost four rounds here.

Seven review rounds were spent hardening a design the author discarded the next day - a cheap architectural gut-check before entering the review loop would have dominated every per-finding improvement on this PR.

evidence: safeAwait only swallows thrown errors, and the code set subscriptionsRegistered = true after the loop regardless of each CommandResponse.success, so a `{success:false}` subscribe would latch the one-shot flag and permanently stop retries on later ready edges. The premise is verifiable from the hunk itself.
guidance_note: When a one-shot registered flag exists to gate retries, set it from the responses' success values, not from the mere absence of a thrown error.

evidence: reconcile() caught an enumerateSessions throw, logged, and returned, after which connect() still projected status `no-sessions` - so a missing tmux binary or a permission error rendered in the debug UI as an empty but healthy mesh. The agent split fatal enumerate failure onto `closed` with the underlying reason.
guidance_note: Keep `the world is empty` and `we failed to look at the world` as distinct states when projecting a status; a catch-and-return that falls through into an empty-state projection collapses them.

evidence: Checked master at HEAD (20 commits and three days past this merge): ownedSessionIds still has no `.add` anywhere in the tree, so the kill-session loop in close() is unreachable, and the only test naming it - `close() leaves non-owned sessions alone (no ownership = no cleanup)` - asserts the vacuous case. The agent's defence quotes the ticket and the repo's carrying-cost doctrine, but the create path it was waiting for never arrived.
guidance_note: A Set with no writer is not a typed boundary an obligation flows through - add the field in the commit that adds the producer, and let the ticket text stay a plan until then.

evidence: The hunk shows `reconnectAttempts: 0, observedSessions: 0,` on one physical line in a multi-property object literal, which Prettier reformats; the agent ran `npm run format` repo-wide and reported it also caught unrelated pre-existing drift. Reply-hint said pushback but the reply is a plain fix.
guidance_note: Run the repo formatter as the last step before pushing a PR branch - two of this PR's five first-round findings were pure format churn that consumed reviewer attention.

evidence: Second instance of the same unformatted one-line object literal, this time in TmuxControlDebug.test.tsx; fixed by the same repo-wide format pass. That the reviewer had to raise it twice shows the pre-push formatter run was skipped, not that the rule was disputed.
guidance_note: Run the formatter before pushing rather than fixing formatting findings one file at a time.

evidence: Real bug: `results.find((r) => r !== null) ?? syntheticOk()` returns success when every client rejected, which combined with F1's one-shot flag means topology subscriptions could latch as registered while no client ever subscribed. Flag is a false positive - I diffed control.ts at b3bf07f and 104802c and the aggregation code is identical; 104802c was the repo-wide Prettier pass, so nothing about this code was fix-caused.
guidance_note: When fanning one command across N peers, decide and encode the aggregation rule (any-success versus all-success, and what an empty peer set means) in the same edit that writes the fan-out.

evidence: Same defect as F6 in unsubscribe(): all-clients-failed returned syntheticOk, so a stale subscription could survive silently. Flag is a false positive for the same verified reason - the unsubscribe body is byte-identical at b3bf07f and at the flagged commit 104802c (a formatting-only commit).
guidance_note: Write the fan-out helper once and route both subscribe and unsubscribe through it, so an aggregation rule cannot be right in one method and wrong in its inverse.

evidence: projectConnectionState took a `reason` parameter, discarded it with `void reason`, and hardcoded `reason: disposed`, so explicit close and fatal enumerate failure were indistinguishable to bridge consumers. Flag is a false positive: `return { status: "closed", reason: "disposed" };` is present at b3bf07f and unchanged through d4097f4 (verified by grepping both trees).
guidance_note: When narrowing a rich internal reason onto a library's small enum, write the case mapping at the moment you write the projection; a parameter deliberately voided is a mapping you have decided not to do.

evidence: The reviewer's stated mechanism is wrong: `let resp;` with a later assignment gets TypeScript's evolving-any treatment and does not error under noImplicitAny, and the agent reported tsc --noEmit already clean - but the fragility point stands and the agent took the reviewer's own second option (const plus .catch, early return on null). Flag is a false positive: `let resp;` is present at line 181 of output-router.ts in b3bf07f, unchanged through the flagged commit 06b5462.
guidance_note: Prefer const plus .catch() to let-then-try/catch for a value assigned once, so the type is visible at the declaration instead of depending on control-flow narrowing.

narrative: Not a single one of the four post-first-round findings was caused by a fix: I diffed control.ts and output-router.ts at b3bf07f against the flagged commits and F6, F7, F8 and F9 all sit on code byte-identical to the pre-review head. The extra rounds came from PR size - 118 files, +3809/-2413, with the reviewer covering 116 of 118 files per round and surfacing different original defects each time. Two of the five first-round findings were Prettier drift the agent could have removed with one pre-push command. The one pushback (F3, dead ownedSessionIds) preserved state that still has no writer at master HEAD.
guidance_observations: An oversized PR buys review rounds directly: this reviewer surfaces a couple of findings per pass regardless of how many real defects the diff contains, so a 118-file diff is structurally a four-round review even when every fix is perfect.
Two round-0 findings and a repo-wide reformat could have been erased by running the formatter before pushing.

The mesh fan-out defects (F6, F7) and the discarded close reason (F8) are all one class - an aggregation or projection over multiple sources written without stating what the multi-source rule is - and all three shipped in the original commit.

evidence: The new integration test wrote a stub with `#!/bin/zsh` and nothing in the repo provisions zsh, so the test would fail for infrastructure reasons on a machine without it; the agent switched to /bin/sh and re-verified empirically that pane_pid stays on the wrapper for its lifetime, which is the property under test.
guidance_note: Write test fixtures against the interpreter the repo already requires (/bin/sh) unless the behavior under test needs a specific shell, and say which property the shell choice is carrying.

evidence: The premise is right: spawnLaunch now marks running immediately after list-panes, so a topology snapshot already in flight can arrive without the new pane and be read as an exit. The agent rejected the reviewer's explicit paneObserved tracking and used `launch.pid !== null` as a proxy on one-source-of-truth grounds - but pid-attached and pane-observed are not the same fact, and the next round (F3) found the exact case where they diverge. Flag is a false positive: gh api shows 27071b7 touched only spawn.integration.test.ts, so the correlator code is original to 7c27d89.
guidance_note: Before reusing an existing field as a proxy for a new predicate, write the accept/reject table for both facts side by side; if any row differs the two are different facts and one-source-of-truth is the wrong argument for merging them.

evidence: The agent's microtask argument does not cover the ordering that matters. In tmux-control-mode-js at the commit contemporaneous with this PR (849a59c, src/client.ts), handleMessage resolves the pending command promise - whose await continuation is queued as a microtask - and then emits notifications synchronously via `this.emitter.emit(msg)`, so a %end for list-panes and a %window-close parsed in the same pass dispatch window-close to the correlator BEFORE spawn's continuation runs registry.create; the correlator's closeHandler iterates listActive() and finds nothing, and the row is then created with pid null against an already-dead pane. `if (launch.pid === null) continue` in reconcileFromSnapshot then leaves it running forever - a stuck state that did not exist before c9164e8, since absence previously always marked exited. The fast-exit integration test passing shows the common interleaving works, not that the coalesced one cannot occur.
guidance_note: When a pushback rests on event ordering, verify the emit path in the library that produces the events - synchronous emit versus promise resolution decides the order, and the await structure of your own function does not.

narrative: Three rounds, three findings, and the third is the audit's target shape: F2's fix introduced the defect F3 reports. The agent declined the reviewer's explicit suggestion to track pane observation and reused `pid !== null` as a proxy, citing one-source-of-truth; the next round showed the two facts diverge for a fast-exiting launch, and the agent pushed back with an event-loop argument that holds for its own function but not for the tmux client's synchronous notification emit. The pushback closed the thread and the code shipped with a launch row that can stay running forever.
guidance_observations: The one-source-of-truth citation did the damage here: it was used to argue two distinct predicates were one fact, and the reviewer's cheaper explicit-flag suggestion would have shipped correct.
A pushback whose whole weight rests on runtime ordering should be required to cite the producing library's dispatch code, not only the shape of the local async function.
Round 2 exists solely because round 1's fix was wrong; a five-minute look at the emit path would have converted both rounds into one correct edit.
